LNP file photo Facebook Twitter Email Print Copy article link A plan to redevelop a former Lititz area pizza restaurant into a commercial building featuring a tower evoking a 15th-century Bohemian castle is getting a $3 million boost from a state-sponsored capital grant program. DTL Partners LLC, a company led by Dan Cicala of Lititz-based construction management firm Fidevia, plans to tear down the 4,300-square-foot La Piazza Italian Restaurant & Bar at 800 Lititz Pike. In its place, the firm will build an 8,500-square-foot building with room for several tenants. The planned brick-and-stone building will include a tower modeled after Castle Litice, a fortress in the modern-day Czech Republic that inspired the Moravian founders of Lititz when naming the town. The redevelopment along Lititz Pike in Warwick Township is one of 16 redevelopment projects in Lancaster County set to receive a combined $40 million through the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program. Gov. Josh Shapiro announced funding for the projects last week. Three of the projects, totaling $18.25 million, were announced by Shapiro in March. State legislators recommend projects for RACP grants, which are awarded at the governor’s discretion. The projects are authorized in the Redevelopment Assistance section of a Capital Budget Itemization Act and are intended to have a regional or multijurisdictional impact while generating substantial increases or maintaining current levels of employment, tax revenue or other economic activity. RACP projects are state-funded projects that cannot obtain primary funding under other state programs. A state timeline for the program notes that grant funds are typically released 19 to 24 months after applicants accept the award—a process that includes a state consultant assigned to each project. Crossings at Penn Ridge, Millersville Borough: $2 million for site work for a planned 350-unit mixed-use housing development at routes 741 and 999. Grant request: $3.5 million. Ephrata Electric Division Facility, Ephrata Borough: $2 million for site work and construction of a new municipal building for the borough’s electric division, which supplies electricity to residents. https://english.radio.cz/ano-support-fal.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК ANO support falls as STAN gains in latest poll Facebook Twitter Support for the ruling ANO party has fallen further, according to a new Kantar election model for Czech Television. ANO would receive 30.5 percent of the vote, down from 34.5 percent in February. The STAN party has gained ground to 17 percent, while ODS remains at 15.5 percent. The Pirates would receive 8.5 percent, SPD 6.5 percent and the Motorists five percent. The survey also found widespread dissatisfaction with Czech politics, with 68 percent of respondents describing the current political situation as either rather or very bad. Kantar surveyed around 1,000 people in August.
